To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the degeneration or the inhibition of dopaminergic neurotransmission in rat striatum results in the increase in the catecholamine (CA)-sensitive Na+,K+-adenosine triphosphatase (ATPase) activity in the striatal microsomes.

the striatum microsomal Na+,K+-adenosine triphosphatase (ATPase) is inhibited by catecholamines and that the catecholamine sensitivity of the enzyme is enhanced in striata with denervated nigrostriatal dopaminergic neurons.
the striatum microsomal Na+,K+-adenosine triphosphatase (Na+,K+-AT-Pase) activity was significantly increased by electrolytic or chemical lesions of the nigrostriatal dopaminergic system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of catecholamines in the regulation of the Na+,K+-activated adenosine triphosphatase (Na+,K+-AT-Pase) activity of the rat striatal microsomes.
the changes in Na+, K+-ATPase, adenylate cyclases, catecholamine receptors and cyclic AMP content of rat striatum following electrolytic or chemical lesions of nigrostriata dopamine (DA) neurons.
the development and the mechanism of supersensitivity to catecholamines in the rat striatal neurons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the supersensitivity of caudate neurons to DA is not due to a change in cyclic AMP formation but to an alteration in postsynaptic DA receptors.
the supersensitivity of caudate neurons to DA is not a result of the increase of DA receptor number, but is due to the increase of the sensitivity of adenylate-cyclase-coupled receptors.
the supersensitivity of the caudate neuron to DA is due to an increased sensitivity of adenylatecyclase system to DA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the postsynaptic supersensitive state to inhibitory action on cyclic AMP accumulation by DA in the caudeate nucleus following 6-OHDA treatment is associated with the increase of DA receptor sites and the decrease of the activity of Na+,K+-dependent adenosinetriphosphatase (Na+,K+-ATPage) in the caudal nucleus (8–10).
the development of supersensitive responses to DA in the striatal neurons is not necessarily dependent upon the cyclic AMP system.

the adenylate cyclases in striatal membranes are not involved in the development of postsynaptic supersensitiviy to DA in the rat caudate neurons, but the Na+,K+-activated ATPase is involved in the supersensitivity (11).
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can now use this method to study the effect of a drug on a particular neurotransmitter system.
the brain has a very high capacity to compensate for damage.
the brain is a very complex and dynamic system.
